Adjacent Incircles

GeometryCirclesTriangles
What it shows: Triangles sharing one top point, each with a circle tucked inside it.
How to play: Drag the dots along the bottom line, or focus a dot and use the arrow keys. Add or remove dots to make more triangles.
Look for the math

Move the bottom points and the circles change. Yet if the small neighbouring circles happen to be the same size, something surprising happens to all the bigger ones.

A fan of triangles

One point A sits above a straight line holding the points M1, M2, .... Each pair of neighbours makes a triangle with A, and each triangle has an incircle. Those are the level 1 circles. Taking points two gaps apart gives the level 2 circles, three gaps apart the level 3 circles, and so on. The applet shows the higher levels only when level 1 matches.

The number that stays the same

Let h be the altitude from A to the line, and for each point let g = (AM + offset from the foot of the altitude) / h. A short calculation gives

r(level 1 at Mi) = h/2 × (1 − g(i)/g(i+1))

So equal level 1 radii mean the numbers g(i) form a geometric progression: each one is the previous one times the same q. This is the invariant behind the picture.

Why the bigger triangles match

For a triangle spanning k gaps the same formula uses g(i)/g(i+k) = q−k, so its radius is h/2 × (1 − q−k) — independent of i. That is exactly the Equal Incircles Theorem on the original page: equal level 1 circles force equal level 2, level 3 and every later level. The logic test confirms it over many fans. It also confirms the wider Demir–Tabov version there: if level 1 radii merely match in pairs two apart, level 2 still comes out equal. Honsberger's restriction to groups of a power of two is narrower than necessary.

The wooden tablet, and a quirk

The 1897 tablet asks for the tangent from the top point when two neighbouring circles are equal. With a the whole bottom side of the two-triangle fan and s its semiperimeter, the page's answer AM2 = √(s(s − a)) checks out. Two honest warnings: equal radii do not make neighbouring bottom lengths equal (try q = 2); and the old applet wrapped its point list, drawing one extra triangle across the whole fan, which hides its own "equal circles" signal. This page follows the fan the page describes instead.

Try Make incircles equal, then move one bottom point a little: watch every level change at once. Then change the number of points while the circles still match.
